comparison: Perfect agreement on dataset claims (C1-C12). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the data provenance and processing well-documented and supported. All three peer reviewers explicitly affirm the use of published data.

Strong agreement on direction angle metric and volume growth findings (C13-C18, C21-C22). Both evaluations find the results convincing and well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes model-independence and consistency across datasets; peer reviewers describe findings as 'rigorous' and 'solid.'

Partial overlap on claims C19-C20 (simulation comparisons). OpenEval includes these in the direction angle analysis (R2) while peer reviewers implicitly accept them as part of the overall volume growth conclusion without specific comment.

Agreement on reanalysis of prior work (C23-C25), but with different confidence levels. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to reliance on appendix materials not fully accessible, while peer reviewers accept the reconciliation as SUPPORTED without raising concerns about the reanalysis methodology.

Perfect agreement on spatial dispersion metric (C26-C32). Both evaluations find the quantitative analysis well-supported with appropriate statistical methods. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the dispersion findings as 'convincing.'

Strong agreement on mechanistic explanation (C33-C43). Both evaluations support the link between tissue mechanics and observed dispersion patterns. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly highlights the role of external forces; OpenEval notes the argument is reasonable but could benefit from more rigorous demonstration.

Agreement on sampling strategy implications (C44-C46). Both evaluations accept this as a logical consequence of volume growth and dispersion. Peer reviewers implicitly accept as part of 'thorough analysis' without specific comment.

Partial overlap on parameter inference (C47-C48). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to wide confidence intervals and model assumptions, while peer reviewers find it SUPPORTED and highlight the high death rate as an 'intriguing phenomenon' with significant impact.

Partial overlap on claim C49 (confidence intervals). OpenEval expresses uncertainty about parameter robustness, while peer reviewers accept the inference methodology as rigorous without raising concerns.

Agreement on reconciliation with prior work (C50-C51), but different confidence levels. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN wanting more transparent presentation in main text, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the explanation as part of overall 'convincing' results.

Overlap on mutation rate comparison (C56). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to calculation dependencies and cross-tissue comparisons, while peer reviewers accept without raising specific concerns about this estimate.

Perfect agreement on mutational signature analysis (C57-C64). Both evaluations find the temporal heterogeneity analysis well-supported with appropriate statistical significance. Peer reviewers accept as part of 'thorough' and 'rigorous' analysis.

Strong agreement on temporal scope inference (C65-C68, C78). Both evaluations accept the population genetics approach for estimating early tumor development timeframes. Peer reviewers explicitly note insights into 'initial phase of tumor expansion.'

Partial overlap on volume growth conclusion (C74). Both strongly support this central finding. OpenEval emphasizes multiple independent lines of evidence; peer reviewers describe as 'convincing' and 'solid' with all three reviewers explicitly affirming.

Partial overlap on high death rate and biological interpretation (C75-C77). OpenEval supports with caveats about model assumptions; peer Reviewer 2 highlights as key finding with significant impact on understanding cancer development.

Perfect agreement on forward-looking statements (C79-C80). Both evaluations accept these as reasonable extrapolations. OpenEval notes they are appropriately framed as speculative; peer reviewers see them as opening 'exciting avenues' for future research.

Perfect agreement on metric properties (C81-C82). Both evaluations affirm the model-independence and robustness to selection. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly praises the 'metrics of interest' as 'chosen in an appropriate manner.'

Perfect agreement on computational model (C84-C98). Both evaluations strongly support the off-lattice modeling approach. OpenEval finds it appropriate for testing spatial predictions; peer reviewers praise the 'particularly nice and tractable cell-based model' enabling thorough analysis.
